newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIAN BANKS FURIOUS AT RUSSIA ACCOUNT FREEZE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIAN BANKS FURIOUS AT RUSSIA ACCOUNT FREEZE.

text.p: The Latvian bank association on Wednesday joined a chorus of protests against a decision by the Russian tax authorities to block Baltic correspondent bank accounts in St Petersburg.

The Association of Latvian Commercial Banks said the tax police had blocked the correspondent accounts for non-payment of value added tax (VAT), which should have been paid by Russian firms when settling payments via Baltic banks.
The exact number of banks that have had their accounts blocked is not known, but most of them are Latvian.

"These events, in our opinion, are a violation of Russian legislation and a breach of international rights," the bank association said in a statement. It said the banks worked in line with their domestic legislation and with Russia.
"Therefore, to speak about paying VAT to the budget of another country is not only senseless but absurd," it said.
It said the banks are appealing the decision in a court of arbitration in St Petersburg and it was convinced the seizure of the accounts would be reversed.

"We believe that these activities can cause serious damage to the links between Russia and Latvia and will also affect the image of Russia that has been formed by the Russian government as a civilised country with a market economy where the spirit of law rules," the association added.
